maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC rollouts service-A started failing with AccessDenied from KMS on decrypt. Noticed ~06:12 UTC. Anyone seen this pattern?

devon: @maya can you paste the CloudTrail deny event or role ARN?

maya: role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/serviceA-worker
CloudTrail snippet:
```
errorCode: "AccessDenied"
errorMessage: "User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/serviceA-worker/session-abc is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01"
```

chris: Did we flip the key policy to require `aws:PrincipalTag/sa` after the rotation? That will deny sessions without that tag.

maya: We did add a condition: `StringEquals: { "aws:PrincipalTag/sa": "true" }` to lock it down. I assumed session tags would be present.

olivia: Confirming the RBAC change earlier — we made tag-based enforcement the rule. If the assume-role call didn't pass session tags, the principal won't have `sa` and the condition will fail.

devon: Quick repro I ran:
```
# assume role WITHOUT tags
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/serviceA-worker --role-session-name test-session
# try decrypt
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ce.dat --key-id alias/mykey --query Plaintext
# -> AccessDenied
```
If I call assume-role with `--tags Key=sa,Value=true` it still failed for me earlier.

chris: Two gotchas to check: 1) Caller must be allowed to pass session tags (and the assume API must include the tags). 2) The role needs `TransitiveTagKeys` set so session tags propagate to downstream services. Without transitive keys the tag appears on the session but isn't usable in conditions like `aws:PrincipalTag`.

maya: I inspected the role config — the trust policy and permissions looked fine, but `TransitiveTagKeys` on the role was empty. So tags weren't transitive.

anna: Also remember KMS evaluates `aws:PrincipalTag` against the request principal (the assumed-role session). If the session doesn't have the tag the key policy condition will deny. CloudTrail shows the deny reason referencing the missing `aws:PrincipalTag/sa`.

security-bot: Note: some SDK credential providers won't include session tags unless the assume step explicitly passes them. When migrating from long-lived creds to assume-role wrappers we sometimes forget to forward tags.

olivia: Proposed immediate fixes: add `sa` to the role's `TransitiveTagKeys` and update our assume-role wrapper to pass session tags for service accounts. Short-term rollback option: relax the key policy to allow the role ARN to `kms:Decrypt` without the tag condition until rollout completes.

devon: I patched staging earlier: added `TransitiveTagKeys: ["sa"]` and re-ran the assume-role with `--tags Key=sa,Value=true` -> `kms:Decrypt` succeeded. I'll open the prod PR with the same change + a test.

maya: Thanks. I also created a ticket to update docs/our assume-role wrapper to always forward `sa=true` for service account sessions, and added a CloudTrail metric filter for KMS AccessDenied events mentioning `aws:PrincipalTag` so we alert faster.

chris: One more note: if we relied on KMS grants pre-rotation those could have masked the issue. We removed old grants during rotation, so the key policy condition became the effective gate. Keep that in mind for future rotations.

maya: Good catch. I'll add a step in the rotation runbook to check existing grants and test tag propagation before revoking old grants.

olivia: All right — prod PR + docs + alerting tracked. Closing the loop once deploys are in. :thumbsup:
